name: MALAWI

flag.title: Flag of Malawi
flag.note: Black, red & green; rising sun added 2010

lead: Malawi is a small country in Southern Africa with no sea coast. One-fifth of it is water. Its people are famous for their smiles. That is why it is called the Warm Heart of Africa.

sections.geography: A lake as big as a sea

geo: Malawi is long and thin. It is nearly 900 km from north to south. It is never wider than 150 km. Lake Malawi fills the deep Great Rift Valley (a giant crack in the land) and is 584 km long.
In the south, Mulanje Massif rises above green tea farms. It is a huge block of granite (hard rock). The Shire River carries lake water south to the Zambezi.
animals: Lake Malawi has over 1,000 kinds of cichlid fish. They shine in every colour. The African fish eagle, Malawi's national bird, hunts along the shore.
Liwonde National Park has 600 elephants and 2,500 hippos. Lions and black rhinos came back there. Nile crocodiles rest on the sandbanks.
culture: The Chewa people perform the Great Dance, Gule Wamkulu. Masked dancers play spirits and wild animals. UNESCO named it world heritage in 2005.
Nsima is a stiff maize porridge. People eat it at nearly every meal, scooped up by hand. Songs fill daily life, played on the mambilira, a wooden xylophone.
history: A jawbone found here in 1991 is 2.4 million years old. In the 1850s, Scottish explorer David Livingstone arrived and mapped the great lake.
Britain made Malawi a colony called Nyasaland in 1891. Hastings Banda led it to independence on 6 July 1964. Democracy came in 1994.
wows: Lake Malawi has more fish species than any other lake.
A 2.4-million-year-old jawbone found here is among the oldest bones of early humans ever found.
One-fifth of Malawi is water, mostly Lake Malawi.
The money, the kwacha, means dawn in Chichewa, for a new day of freedom.
Liwonde Park brought back lions, cheetahs, wild dogs and black rhinos all within one decade.
Gule Wamkulu dancers belong to a secret society hundreds of years old.
In 2012 President Joyce Banda sold the presidential jet for $15 million to fund the national budget.

myths.myth: Lake Malawi is salty like the sea
myths.fact: No, its water is fresh. It is the third-largest freshwater lake in Africa.
Africa has 54 countries. Malawi is one of them, with its own flag and money.
